newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise after U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise after U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher in late trading Tuesday in pursuit of the U.S. Treasuries market, traders said.
"There was a high volume of trade today, with spreads between local bonds and Treasuries basically staying pretty much the same," said one trader.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to 94-1/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 added $0.26 to 121.28.
Buying by institutional investors helped pump up volumes in a market which also drew encouragement from continuing growth in the Argentine economy, traders said.
